author: Horsfield, 1821
summary: 봄과 가을에 우리나라를 흔하게 지나가는 나그네새로, 간척지·염전·하구·삼각주·논 등에 내려앉는다. 갑각류와 곤충을 먹고 때로는 식물성 먹이도 먹는다. 시베리아 동북부의 툰드라와 캄차카에서 번식하고 오스트레일리아, 뉴질랜드 등에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: black spots on breast and flanks

art.subject: Sharp-tailed Sandpiper (Calidris acuminata), adult in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean flooded paddies in late April-May: bright rufous cap finely streaked black, contrasting with a whitish supercilium that is broadest behind the eye; thin white eye-ring; face and neck buff-white with fine dark streaks; mantle, scapulars and tertials black-centred with rufous, buff and whitish fringes; breast buff, densely marked with dark spots that become bold dark arrowhead (chevron) marks on the lower breast and along the flanks to the undertail coverts; belly white; bill dark grey-black with a paler greyish-olive base; dark eye; greenish-yellow to olive legs.
art.pose: foraging in a wet rice field, side view
art.scene: Korean flooded rice paddies near an estuary in May, during spring migration, shallow water and mud; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding, side view standing in shallow water: rufous cap, whitish supercilium, rufous-and-black upperparts, buff breast with dark spots turning into chevrons along the flanks, white belly, greenish-yellow legs

adult breeding, head detail in side view: rufous crown and hindneck finely streaked black, whitish supercilium broadening behind the eye, thin white eye-ring, slightly drooping dark bill with a paler base
art.build: Medium-small sandpiper, about 21cm, about the size of a Common Starling but on longer legs; plump body, small head, medium-length neck. Bill dark, slightly shorter than the head, straight with a faint droop near the tip. Legs medium-long, greenish-yellow. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. Tail wedge-shaped with pointed central feathers. In flight a thin white wing-bar and a dark centre to the rump and tail with white sides.
avoid: Do not paint a heavily streaked breast ending in a sharp line against a white belly - that is Pectoral Sandpiper (Calidris melanotos); here dark chevrons spread down the flanks.
Do not paint black legs or a long curved bill.
Do not give it a plain grey-brown crown; the cap is rufous.
